question: Who killed Goliath?
summary: 1 Samuel 17 credits David with killing Goliath of Gath. 2 Samuel 21:19 says Elhanan son of Jaare-oregim killed Goliath the Gittite, identifying Goliath specifically by the same weapon-description ("the staff of whose spear was like a weaver's beam") used for Goliath in 1 Samuel 17:7. The Chronicler in 1 Chronicles 20:5 "fixes" the problem by inserting "the brother of" before Goliath's name — a transparent harmonization.

reconcile.connective: Defenders read 2 Samuel 21:19 as a copyist's slip, restoring "brother of Goliath" from the parallel in 1 Chronicles 20:5 so David remains the giant's slayer.

discrepancy.connective: Baruch Halpern presses that the Masoretic text of 2 Samuel 21:19 plainly has Elhanan kill Goliath with no "brother" in it, so the Chronicler's added phrase is itself the harmonizing fix, not the original reading.

pd_work.note: Clarke treats this exact verse, calling it a transcriber's corruption and restoring the 1 Chronicles 20:5 reading (Lahmi, brother of Goliath) on the authority of Kennicott so that David, not Elhanan, slew Goliath.

excerpts.excerpt_text: the word "brother" is rightly supplied from Ch1 20:5; where his name is said to be Lahmi, for not Goliath himself was slain, though some so interpret it, and take Elhanan to be David; so Jarchi, and with which agrees the Targum; but he was slain not at Gob, but in the valley of Elah, nor had David any such name as Elhanan …
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly answers 'Who killed Goliath?' by harmonizing 2 Sam 21:19 with 1 Sam 17 via the Chronicler's 'brother' (Lahmi), denying Elhanan=David and that Goliath himself was slain here. Strongest single reconcile; parity-capped to one on this discrepancy_first row.
excerpts.source_note_text:
And there was again a battle in Gob with the Philistines,.... Another battle with them in the same place:
where Elhanan the son of Jaareoregim, a Bethlehemite, slew the brother of Goliath the Gittite; the word "brother" is rightly supplied from Ch1 20:5; where his name is said to be Lahmi, for not Goliath himself was slain, though some so interpret it, and take Elhanan to be David; so Jarchi, and with which agrees the Targum; but he was slain not at Gob, but in the valley of Elah, nor had David any such name as Elhanan; he was one of David's worthies, Sa2 23:24; where he is called the son of Dodo, and in Ch1 20:5, the son of Jair; and Lahmi there may not be the name of Goliath's brother, but, as here, the country name of Elhanan; for the words (z) there may be rendered,"and Elhanan the son of Jair, the Lehemite (i.e. the Bethlehemite), slew the brother of Goliath the Gittite,''and so perfectly agrees, with this:
the staff of whose spear was like a weaver's beam; not of Goliath's brother, but of Goliath himself, Sa1 17:7.
(z) Vid. Buxtorf. Anticritic. par. 2. c. 2. p. 421.
